## What this book is

*Collective Predictive Coding* (CPC) is presented here as a **mathematical theory of symbol
emergence systems**. The book has three aims:

1. To give CPC a systematic mathematical formulation as a theory of symbol emergence systems.
2. To unify formulations that are currently scattered across individual papers, deriving them
   as successive elaborations of a **single generative model**.
3. To be usable as a foundational text beyond robotics — for CPC-MS and, more broadly, for
   theories of symbol systems and intelligence.

## Positioning

CPC is not a theory of *symbol emergence*. It is a theory of **symbol emergence systems**.
Its object is not only the process by which symbols arise, but the *system* in which the
cognitive dynamics of individuals and the dynamics of a society's symbol system organize
each other.

Three terms are kept distinct throughout the book:

| Term | What it refers to |
|---|---|
| **Symbol system** | The **product** of emergence. Corresponds to $w$. |
| **Symbol emergence** | The **process** by which it arises. |
| **Symbol emergence system** | The **system** in which that process takes place. |

The Springer book *Symbol Emergence Systems* discusses what such systems are and how they
look as a whole; this book supplies their mathematics. The two are companion volumes.

This book is **not** a general survey of symbol emergence in robotics. Not repeating the
structure of *Symbol Emergence in Robotics* is an explicit constraint on its design.

### Intended readers

- **Primary:** graduate students and researchers in informatics, cognitive science, and robotics.
- **Secondary:** graduate students in linguistics, anthropology, sociology, science studies,
  and economics.

Variational Bayes is assumed as the lower bound of mathematical background; mathematical
preliminaries are collected in the appendices rather than in the main text.

## The core formulation

The whole book is organized around one generative model,

$$
p(w) \prod_{k=1}^{K} p(z_k \mid w)\, p(x_k \mid z_k),
$$

and the collective posterior it induces,

$$
P(w \mid x_{1:K}) \;\propto\; p(w) \prod_{k=1}^{K} \int p(x_k \mid z_k)\, p(z_k \mid w)\, \mathrm{d}z_k .
$$

Two constraints give this model its meaning:

**Operational closure.** Agent $k$ has no access whatsoever to $z_j$ for $j \neq k$.

**Arbitrariness.** The relation between $w$ and $z$ is not an invertible map but a general
probabilistic relation $P(w \mid z)$. Dimensions and types need not agree, and $w$ may be
discrete or continuous.

Chapters 1 and 2 state this formulation. Every later chapter can be read as a commentary on
Chapter 2 — extensions are presented as *differences* from it: put $w_{1:T}$ into the
equation, multiply in an optimality-variable term, let $w$ be continuous.

Each chapter is built around a single proposition, typically of the form: *language game $G$
is a correct inference algorithm for the posterior of generative model $\mathcal{M}$.* The
theory is the collection of these propositions.

## How to read it

Readers who do not want to follow the mathematics can read

> **Chapters 1–2 → Chapter 13 → Chapter 24 → Part VI → Chapter 31**

and skip the rest. This is a legitimate path through the book, not a shortcut.
Every chapter opens with an intuitive summary in one paragraph and no equations,
Appendix D gives a correspondence table between humanities/social-science and mathematical
vocabulary, and Part VI does not depend on Part II.

## Status

Writing volume and verification are tracked as **two separate axes**. They are not combined
into a single percentage, because drafting can run ahead of checking.

**Writing volume** — ⬜ not started / ◽ outline only / ◨ partially written / ⬛ full draft

**Verification** — 🤖 raw AI output (*correctness not guaranteed in any way*) /
👀 visually checked / ✅ author-verified

::: {.callout-warning title="Current status"}
**All chapters are between ⬜ and ◽, and all are 🤖.** Nothing on this site has been
verified by the author. Per-chapter status badges will be added as writing begins.
:::

## Comments and corrections

Corrections and suggestions are welcome — typographical errors, mistakes in the mathematics,
and proposals for the content alike. Comments may be written in **English or Japanese**.

- **Open an issue:** <https://github.com/tanichu/cpc-textbook/issues>

Terms, in brief:

- The author reserves the right to reflect any comment or suggestion in the published book.
  No compensation or claim of co-authorship arises from making one.
- Contributors will be named in the acknowledgements.

Additional channels (threaded discussion attached to each chapter, inline annotation, an
anonymous form) are under consideration and are not yet available.
